I ndian Economic Overview The Indian economy recorded strong growth during FY 2025-26, with GDP expanding by around 6.5%-7.0%, supported by robust domestic demand and sustained government capital expenditure.
Margins & costs: 58.60 crore, with the EBITDA margin moderating by approximately 101 basis points to 11.8% from 12.8% on revenue from operations.

Suppliers, particularly smaller vendors, sought price increases as their own material, labour, energy and operating costs rose; the Company was unable to pass these increases on to large customers with the same speed - the resulting time gap between supplier cost escalation and customer price revision, placing a direct pressure on margins.
Inflation moderated during the year to approximately 4.2%-4.4%, supported by easing commodity prices, though core inflation remained elevated due to persistent services demand and wage pressures.
Capex & expansion: Employee benefit expenses increased by 5.28% to H6,660.99 lakhs, reflecting continued investment in human resources, while depreciation and amortisation expenses increased by 24.13% to H2,133.60 lakhs due to capital expenditure undertaken during the year.
